name: Is my PDF uploaded anywhere to convert it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Every slide is rendered and packaged in your browser using pdf.js and PptxGenJS. Your PDF never leaves your device.

name: Does PDFree store or log my files after processing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree runs entirely in your browser — there is no backend server that receives your files. Because nothing is uploaded, nothing can be stored, logged, or retained. Your document exists only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session and is cleared when you close the tab.

name: Can I edit the text on the slides after converting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — with Editable text, the default mode, the slide keeps the page's look — photos, charts and table lines included — and all of its text becomes real, editable text boxes in the same place, size and colour; text on scanned pages is read with OCR. In Image mode each slide is one picture of the page and its text is not editable. For a fully editable document, use PDF to Word.

name: What size will my slides be?

acceptedAnswer.text: The deck's slide size matches your PDF's first-page dimensions and aspect ratio. If every page is the same size, slides fill edge-to-edge with no letterboxing. PowerPoint only supports one slide size per deck, so if your PDF mixes page sizes or orientations, those pages are scaled to fit and centered instead of being stretched or distorted.

name: Which quality setting should I choose?

acceptedAnswer.text: Balanced (150 dpi) is a good default for most decks. Choose High quality for dense text or fine print; choose Compact if you're emailing the file and want a smaller size.

name: Is this a free PDF to PowerPoint converter with no sign up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree is completely free — no sign up, no account, no installation. Open the tool, load your PDF, and download the .pptx file.

name: Will this work with a large PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, though very large page counts automatically use a lower image quality to keep your browser from running out of memory. For huge decks, Compact quality is the most reliable choice.

name: Can I put one question per slide, for a quiz or a worksheet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose your PDF and press One question per slide. Draw a frame around each question — the Suggest frames help reads the numbers on single-column pages, and a picture or instructions shared by several questions can be attached to all of them. Each slide shows its question exactly as on the page, cut from it, with as much space to work as you choose. Turn on Interactive answer to make A–E choices clickable in the slide show: a correct answer shows your explanation, a wrong one says Try again. You can also download a PDF with one question per page for printing. Everything happens in your browser; the PDF is not uploaded.
